subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: Should Darwin gateway exec auto-run matched allowlist commands when the enforced-command renderer rejects shell expansion or wrapper payloads, or should that remain an explicit-approval boundary?
rationale: Relaxing the gate could restore documented automation, but the current code treats unenforceable shell expansion as a security boundary because the gateway cannot pin the exact resolved command safely.

options.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shell shapes
options.body: Add a narrow safe renderer for common forms such as tilde expansion where the resolved argv can be pinned, keep approval for genuinely unenforceable forms, and add macOS-focused regression proof.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep the current approval gate and update exec approval docs plus warning text to say shell-shaped Darwin commands may require approval even after an allowlist match.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell commands
options.body: Bypass the enforced-command requirement for matched allowlist commands, accepting broader shell-resolution risk for automation.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shell shapes
recommendation.body: Add a narrow safe renderer for common forms such as tilde expansion where the resolved argv can be pinned, keep approval for genuinely unenforceable forms, and add macOS-focused regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant gateway approval and durable trust history is concentrated in Vincent Koc's remote approval regression work.
